description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 layers in a layered mixture-of-experts model, with the vertical axis representing the "Number of Experts" on a linear scale from 0 to 10 and the horizontal axis showing the "Layer" number from 1 to 24. Each stacked bar corresponds to a layer and is composed of three colored segments: a blue segment at the bottom (labeled G1), a green segment in the middle, and a yellow segment at the top (labeled G2), as indicated by the legend. The total number of experts per layer is the sum of the heights of these three segments. The chart shows that the number of experts varies significantly across layers, with the highest total occurring at Layer 1 (approximately 9 experts), followed by Layer 2 (approximately 8 experts) and Layer 4 (approximately 8 experts). The number of experts generally decreases after Layer 5, with a notable dip around Layer 10 (approximately 4 experts), before increasing again in the latter half of the model. The distribution of the three expert types (G1, G2, and the green segment) also varies per layer, with the green segment often being the largest component, while the blue (G1) and yellow (G2) segments are smaller and more consistent in height across most layers.
